rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report disconnected because al-Hasan did not meet Umar; he understands it to mean Umar initiated collection and supervised its preservation and compilation.
rows.anchor: هذا منقطع، فإن الحسن لم يدرك عمر، ومعناه: أشار بجمعه فجمع

rows.speaker: يحيى بن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب
rows.claim: Yahya reports that Umar would accept no Qur'anic material for the collection without two witnesses.
rows.anchor: عن يحيى بن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب، أن عمر لما جمع القرآن كان لا يقبل من أحد شيئا حتى يشهد شاهدان

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: Urwa reports that Abu Bakr feared the Qur'an would be lost after many reciters were killed and ordered Umar and Zayd to write any material supported by two witnesses; Ibn Kathir grades the disconnected report fair.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه قال: لما استحر القتل بالقراء يومئذ فرق أبو بكر، رضي الله عنه، أن يضيع

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd says he found the ending of Surat al-Tawba with Abu Khuzayma al-Ansari, also identified in a report as Khuzayma b. Thabit, and no one else; they wrote it because the Prophet had counted Khuzayma's testimony as two.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال زيد بن ثابت: وجدت آخر سورة التوبة، يعني قوله تعالى: {لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم}

rows.speaker: خزيمة بن ثابت
rows.claim: Khuzayma's testimony was counted as two after he affirmed the Prophet's purchase of a horse when its Bedouin seller denied the sale.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية: مع خزيمة بن ثابت الذي جعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شهادته بشهادتين لم أجدها مع غيره

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliyah reports that Ubayy b. Ka'b dictated the two verses to the collectors together with Khuzayma b. Thabit.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع عن أبي العالية أن أبي بن كعب أملاها عليهم مع خزيمة بن ثابت

rows.speaker: يحيى بن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب
rows.claim: Yahya also reports that Uthman testified to the same material found for the collection.
rows.anchor: عن يحيى ابن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب؛ أن عثمان شهد بذلك أيضا

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd describes gathering the Qur'an from palm stalks, flat stones, and the memories of men; another wording lists sheets, shoulder blades, and camel gear.
rows.anchor: وأما قول زيد [بن ثابت] (2) "فتتبعت القرآن أجمعه من العسب واللخاف وصدور الرجال"

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: Uthman explains that the Prophet placed revealed verses in designated surahs; Anfal came early in Medina and Bara'a late, their stories were similar, and the Prophet died without clarifying whether Bara'a belonged with Anfal, so Uthman joined them without basmala among the seven long surahs.
rows.anchor: وكانت الأنفال من أول ما نزل بالمدينة، وكانت براءة من آخر القرآن، وكانت قصتها شبيهة بقصتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir infers that the order of verses and surahs was transmitted from the Prophet, while the arrangement of surahs in the codex was Uthman's work; reciting in reverse order is a serious error.
rows.anchor: ففهم من هذا الحديث أن ترتيب الآيات والسور أمر توقيفي متلقى عن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأما ترتيب السور فمن أمير المؤمنين عثمان بن عفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Uthman's surah sequence is recommended; continuous recitation as the Prophet did is preferable, though separating surahs is permitted, as shown by his Friday and Eid recitations.
rows.anchor: وأما ترتيب السور فمستحب اقتداء بعثمان، رضي الله عنه، والأولى إذا قرأ أن يقرأ متواليا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that the material people call al-Mufassal is al-Muhkam, and that he had read it by the Prophet's death at age ten.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: توفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا ابن عشر سنين وقد قرأت المحكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports collecting al-Muhkam during the Prophet's lifetime and identifies al-Muhkam as al-Mufassal; al-Bukhari alone transmits this report.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: جمعت المحكم في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت له: وما المحكم؟ قال: "المفصل"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir takes the report as evidence that teaching children Qur'an is permissible, and says it may even be recommended or obligatory: early learning equips a child to pray and makes memorization more lasting.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على جواز تعلم الصبيان القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A Bukhari report says Ibn Abbas was circumcised when the Prophet died; since boys were circumcised at puberty, Ibn Kathir allows that he rounded his age down to ten.
rows.anchor: وقد روى البخاري أنه قال: توفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا مختون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some early authorities recommended letting a child play briefly at first, then directing his attention to reading, to avoid making him resent and abandon it.
rows.anchor: وقد استحب بعض السلف أن يترك الصبي في ابتداء عمره قليلا للعب، ثم توفر همته على القراءة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some scholars disliked teaching Qur'an to a child who cannot understand; they advised waiting until discernment, then teaching gradually according to capacity, interest, memory, and intelligence.
rows.anchor: وكره بعضهم تعليمهم القرآن وهو لا يعقل ما يقال له، ولكن يترك حتى إذا عقل وميز علم قليلا قليلا

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar recommended teaching a child five verses at a time; Ibn Kathir says the report has a good chain.
rows.anchor: واستحب عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، أن يلقن خمس آيات خمس آيات، رويناه عنه بسند جيد

rows.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
rows.claim: A report from Usayd says he recited Qur'an in a fine voice on his rooftop, then relates an account like the one that follows.
rows.anchor: عن ابن كعب بن مالك، عن أسيد بن حضير: أنه كان على ظهر بيته يقرأ القرآن وهو حسن الصوت

rows.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
rows.claim: Usayd says that while he recited at night he heard a thud and saw lamp-like lights filling the space between heaven and earth; the Prophet explained that angels had descended for the recitation, and Usayd could have seen wonders if he continued.
rows.anchor: عن أسيد بن حضير قال

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Bara' reports that a man reciting Surat al-Kahf at night saw a cloud-like form above his running horse; the Prophet said sakina had descended for the Qur'an. Ibn Kathir says this apparently was Usayd and notes the unusual suspended form in Bukhari.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق سمع البراء يقول: بينما رجل يقرأ سورة الكهف ليلة إذ رأى دابته تركض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the reports support the chapter's account of sakina and angels descending during Qur'an recitation.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا هو أسيد بن الحضير، رضي الله عنه، فهذا ما يتعلق بصناعة الإسناد

rows.speaker: أشياخ أهل المدينة
rows.claim: Medinan elders reported that Thabit b. Qays's house shone like lamps one night; the Prophet guessed that he had recited al-Baqara, and Thabit confirmed it.
rows.anchor: أن أشياخ أهل المدينة حدثوه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قيل له: ألم تر ثابت بن قيس بن شماس لم تزل داره البارحة تزهر مصابيح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-Muhaymin as the trustworthy Qur'an, entrusted over every earlier scripture; Ibn Kathir relates this to Qur'an 5:48.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: المهيمن الأمين القرآن، أمين على كل كتاب قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari placed Qur'an virtues after tafsir because tafsir is more important; Ibn Kathir instead puts virtues first, including each surah's merit before its commentary, to encourage memorization, understanding, and practice.
rows.anchor: ذكر البخاري، رحمه الله، كتاب "فضائل القرآن" بعد كتاب التفسير؛ لأن التفسير أهم ولهذا بدأ به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains al-Muhaymin as a witness over the preceding scriptures.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية: شهيدا عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report through Sufyan al-Thawri and other leading authorities, Ibn Abbas glosses al-Muhaymin as entrusted over the earlier books.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق السبيعي، عن التميمي، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وقتادة وابن جريج والحسن البصري
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Hasan al-Basri share this entrusted or trustworthy sense of al-Muhaymin.
rows.anchor: وبنحو ذلك قال مجاهد والسدي وقتادة وابن جريج والحسن البصري وغير واحد من أئمة السلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of haymana is guarding and watching; al-Muhaymin as a divine name means witness, overseer, and preserver of everything.
rows.anchor: وأصل الهيمنة: الحفظ والارتقاب، يقال إذا رقب الرجل الشيء وحفظه وشهده

rows.speaker: عائشة وابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Aisha and Ibn Abbas says the Prophet received Qur'an in Mecca for ten years and in Medina for ten; Ibn Kathir says al-Bukhari alone includes it among the two Sahihs, while al-Nasa'i also transmits it from Aisha.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سلمة قال: أخبرتني عائشة وابن عباس قالا لبث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة عشر سنين ينزل عليه القرآن، وبالمدينة عشرا

rows.speaker: السلف
rows.claim: The early Muslims understood singing the Qur'an as improving the voice and reciting with a sorrowful, affecting tone.
rows.anchor: فقد فهم من هذا أن السلف، رضي الله عنهم، إنما فهموا من التغني بالقرآن: إنما هو تحسين الصوت به، وتحزينه

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Bara' reports the Prophet's instruction to beautify the Qur'an with one's voice; Ibn Kathir calls the chain good and notes corroborating routes in al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.
rows.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب قال

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سعيد القطان
rows.claim: Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban regarded Abd al-Rahman b. Awsaja as trustworthy, but al-Azdi reports that Yahya b. Sa'id al-Qattan did not approve of him.
rows.anchor: ونقل الأزدي عن يحيى بن سعيد القطان أنه قال: سألت عنه بالمدينة، فلم أرهم يحمدونه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd reports that Ayub told Shu'ba not to transmit the beautifying-voices hadith; Abu Ubayd supposes Ayub feared people would take it as permission for invented melodies.
rows.anchor: نهاني أيوب أن أحدث بهذا الحديث: "زينوا القرآن بأصواتكم". قال أبو عبيد: وإنما كره أيوب فيما نرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects withholding a sound report merely because someone might misinterpret it: that would discard much Sunnah, just as people have distorted Qur'anic verses from their intended legal senses.
rows.anchor: ولو ترك كل حديث بتأول مبطل لترك من السنة شيء كثير، بل قد تطرقوا إلى تأويل آيات كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautifying recitation means making it melodious and sorrowful, with humility.
rows.anchor: والمراد من تحسين الصوت بالقرآن: تطريبه وتحزينه والتخشع به

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abu Musa says he would have ornamented his recitation had he known the Prophet was listening; Muslim adds the Prophet said he had been given one of David's family's flutes.
rows.anchor: قلت: أما والله لو علمت أنك تستمع قراءتي لحبرتها لك تحبيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir infers that deliberate vocal embellishment is permitted: Abu Musa had a fine voice, marked by deep fear and the Yemenites' tenderness, and the Prophet praised it.
rows.anchor: فدل على جواز تعاطي ذلك وتكلفه، وقد كان أبو موسى كما قال، عليه السلام، قد أعطي صوتا حسنا

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl reports that a man unable to provide even an iron ring married a woman in return for what he knew of the Qur'an; the Prophet instructed him to give her what he had memorized.
rows.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir understands the man to have been required to teach the woman the Qur'an he knew, with that teaching serving as her dower.
rows.anchor: وأمره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يعلمه تلك المرأة، ويكون ذلك صداقا لها على ذلك

rows.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Scholars dispute whether Qur'an teaching may be a dower or earn a fee, whether this ruling was specific, and how to read the marriage formula; Ahmad says it means honoring the man or compensation for what he knew, which Ibn Kathir prefers because Muslim's version says “teach her.”
rows.anchor: كما قاله أحمد بن حنبل: نكرمك بذلك أو بعوض ما معك، وهذا أقوى، لقوله في صحيح مسلم: "فعلمها"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading from a mushaf helps prevent neglect and lets readers recall omissions, detect altered or misplaced words and verses, and verify recitation; for learning exact performance, oral instruction is better because writing alone often leads to errors.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآثار تدل على أن هذا أمر مطلوب لئلا يعطل المصحف فلا يقرأ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If reading from writing causes mispronunciation while a qualified teacher is available, Ibn Kathir says to avoid it; when no teacher can be found, necessity permits reading from the mushaf and one is not charged beyond capacity.
rows.anchor: فأما عند العجز عمن يلقن فلا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها، فيجوز عند الضرورة ما لا يجوز عند الرفاهية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A traveler reportedly traced to the Prophet the statement that when a servant mispronounces or errs while reading, an angel records it as it was revealed; the narrator is uncertain that it is prophetic.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا صحبهم في سفر قال: فحدثنا حديثا ما أعلمه إلا رفعه إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: بكير بن الأخنس
rows.claim: Bakir b. al-Akhnas relates the saying that when a non-Arab or someone unable to recite correctly reads, the angel records it as revealed.
rows.anchor: عن بكير (2) بن الأخنس قال: كان يقال: إذا قرأ الأعجمي والذي لا يقيم القرآن كتبه الملك كما أنزل

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars make the better mode depend on concentration: recite from memory if more attentive, or from a mushaf if that produces greater concentration; if equal, looking at the mushaf is preferable for accuracy and the added act of looking. Al-Nawawi says this best explains the early authorities' practice.
rows.anchor: المدار في هذه المسألة على الخشوع في القراءة، فإن كان الخشوع عند القراءة على ظهر القلب فهو أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-Bukhari meant Sahl's marriage report to prove reciting from memory is always superior, Ibn Kathir objects: it may have been a special case involving an illiterate man and cannot establish a general rule.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن تلاوة القرآن عن ظهر قلب أفضل منها في المصحف، ففيه نظر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that people who gather in a mosque to recite and study Qur'an receive sakina and mercy, are surrounded by angels, and are mentioned by God among those near Him.
rows.anchor: ما اجتمع قوم في بيت من بيوت الله، يتلون كتاب الله، ويتدارسونه فيما بينهم، إلا نزلت عليهم السكينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Qur'an commentators say the dawn recitation is witnessed by angels; a hadith from Abu Hurayra explains that night and day angels meet at dawn and afternoon prayers and report finding the servants praying.
rows.anchor: وجاء في بعض التفاسير: أن الملائكة تشهده. وقد جاء في الصحيحين عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that God's book opens with praise in both al-Fatiha and al-Kahf, citing Qur'an 1:2–4 and 18:1–5.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي افتتح كتابه بالحمد فقال: {الحمد لله رب العالمين * الرحمن الرحيم * مالك يوم الدين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation begins with praise in Qur'an 6:1, and the account of the final destinies ends with praise in 39:75.
rows.anchor: وافتتح خلقه بالحمد، فقال تعالى: {الحمد لله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وجعل الظلمات والنور ثم الذين كفروا بربهم يعدلون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is praised in this life and the next, in all He has created and will create; Qur'an 28:70 and 34:1 express this comprehensive praise.
rows.anchor: فله الحمد في الأولى والآخرة، أي في جميع ما خلق وما هو خالق، هو المحمود في ذلك كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir cites the prayer “Our Lord, to You belongs praise, filling the heavens and earth and whatever else You will” as an expression of praise without limit.
rows.anchor: كما يقول المصلي: "اللهم ربنا لك الحمد، ملء السماوات وملء الأرض، وملء ما شئت من شيء بعد"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise are inspired to glorify and praise God as naturally as breathing because they witness His immense blessings, power, sovereignty, and unending beneficence; Ibn Kathir links this to Qur'an 10:9–10.
rows.anchor: ولهذا يلهم أهل الجنة تسبيحه وتحميده كما يلهمون النفس، أي يسبحونه ويحمدونه عدد أنفاسهم

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy reports that two men recited differently, the Prophet affirmed both, and explained that God progressively permitted one, two, then seven modes; Ubayy used two requests to seek forgiveness for his community and reserved the third as intercession on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: فقال لهما النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "اقرآ"، فقرآ، فقال: "أصبتما". فلما قال لهما النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الذي قال

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: In another report, God commands recitation in seven forms from seven gates of Paradise, each described as healing and sufficient.
rows.anchor: فأمرني أن أقرأه على سبعة أحرف من سبعة أبواب الجنة كلها شاف كاف

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy reports that the Prophet accepted two differing readings of Surat al-Nahl and explained the successive permission for seven forms; Ibn Kathir grades this chain authentic.
rows.anchor: فوجدت في نفسي وسوسة الشيطان حتى احمر وجهي، فعرف ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في وجهي
